text:
lena (sales): FYI — NovaAPI migration POC kicks off tomorrow. Customer requirement: swap their Nova endpoints to Redwood with zero UX regressions for the "search + extract" flow. Must answer pricing parity questions, confirm token accounting differences, and provide a short security write-up for their procurement team. Omar, can you run the technical presales checklist?

omar (solutions): On it. Proposed checklist: 1) endpoint adapter contract (request/response fields) 2) deterministic token counts & sample set 3) canonical prompt envelopes (metadata preservation) 4) error/fallback behavior mapping 5) small A/B harness + metrics 6) pricing scenarios to mirror Nova bundles 7) security answers for procurement.

tia (eng): Adapter plan: small express proxy that accepts Nova-style payloads and returns Redwood responses with the Nova wrappers intact. We'll handle: header mapping, default param translation, and a token normalization pass. Example mapping:```bash
# client -> adapter (Nova format)
POST /nova/v1/infer
{ "q": "<PROMPT>", "limit": 400 }
# adapter -> redwood
POST /v1/respond
{ "input": "<PROMPT>", "max_total_tokens": 400 }
```Token shim will re-tokenize and apply an offset table (we observed systematic +12% tokens on seed set).

alex (security): Procurement wanted to know about KMS and HSM. Quick answers: customer-managed KMS supported in Dedicated & Private; for HSM-backed keys we offer partner integration (procurement/legal loop required). We can export per-customer audit logs (S3 or syslog) and support IP allowlisting for staging. Need to confirm retention windows for logs.

noah (sales-eng): Pricing angle: Nova sells flat-call bundles (e.g., 100k calls/mo). Options to propose: 1) token-equivalent with a 12% delta adjustment 2) flat-call equivalence (estimate average tokens per call) 3) commit + burst (dedicated) with a migration credit month. I suggest we prepare 3 sample invoices for a 50k-call scenario showing cost-neutral and cost-reduced options.

rita (cs): Canary plan & operations: start with synthetic parity tests (1000 prompts), then route 3% live traffic for 24hrs, monitor error rate, exact-match %, and structured extraction accuracy. Failover rule: auto-switch back to Nova if error rate >1% over 5m or extraction accuracy drops >5% vs baseline. We'll capture diffs in a CSV for triage.

omar (solutions): For parity scoring I'll include: token_delta, exact_struct_match (keys/values), normalized_text_similarity (trim/whitespace/punct normalization), and length_delta. We'll ship a tiny node harness that outputs a JSONL of metrics.

tia (eng): Implementation notes on deltas: biggest sources are tokenizer vocabulary (we saw +12%), default sampling (Nova had temp=0.7 implicit), and newline/stop handling. Mitigations: set explicit temperature=0.0 for deterministic outputs in POC, inject explicit stop sequences in adapter, and run a post-normalize pass to unify whitespace.

alex (security): Action for me: fill procurement security sheet with our answers about data residency (we can pin EU region for BlueArc), KMS/HSM (see above), SOC2 status, and network egress IPs for staging. Send me the highlighted procurement questions.

lena (sales): I uploaded the procurement spreadsheet and marked the three redlines: EU residency, HSM proof, and contractual SLA over 99.9% for the POC duration.

noah (sales-eng): I'll prepare the three pricing scenarios and include an example migration credit (e.g., 25% off first-month usage) to offset tokenization delta risk.

rita (cs): deploy-bot: scheduling canary run: nova-adapter -> canary-2026-03-26T08:00Z (3% traffic). CI pipeline will run e2e parity harness before traffic flip.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: nova-adapter/canary -> 2026-03-26T08:00Z (3%). Checks: unit tests, tokenizer-run, parity harness.

omar (solutions): Owners & deadlines: 1) token sample run (200 prompts) -> omar (EOD) 2) adapter stub + mapping doc -> tia (tomorrow 10:00) 3) procurement answers -> alex + legal (tomorrow noon) 4) pricing scenarios -> noah (tomorrow COB) 5) parity harness -> omar + tia (initial by day 1 of POC) 6) canary runbook & failback -> rita (pre-canary).

lena (sales): Let's do a 09:00 sync tomorrow for 15m to make sure nothing blocks. Ping here if you hit legal/security blockers. :rocket:

rita (cs): I'll post the pre-canary checklist in here once it's ready (network rules, healthcheck URLs, monitoring dashboards).

noah (sales-eng): Also flagging the contract team: Nova contracts often request liability language for model hallucinations. Legal will need to own that.

omar (solutions): Noted. I'll include a suggested clause to mirror expected behavior for POC (limited warranty + assist triage during migration).

lena (sales): Great team — thanks.
